action_item_for_main_agent: URGENT FOR TOMORROW'S CLIENT MEETING: Implement missing backend API endpoints for: 1) Finance dashboard (budget/profit calculations), 2) Calendar dashboard (3 timelines with predictions), 3) Reports dashboard (vendor spend, time tracking), 4) Exports dashboard (electrician sheet, load-in sheet, mover's FFE sheet). Current system can handle questionnaire submission and basic project management, but cannot generate the print exports needed for real-world use.

detailed_findings.questionnaire_workflow: ✅ WORKING - Customer can access and fill out comprehensive questionnaire. Form displays all required fields including client info, project details, style preferences, and special requirements.
detailed_findings.project_management: ✅ WORKING - Projects can be created, retrieved, and updated. Questionnaire data successfully populates project fields.
detailed_findings.ffe_spreadsheet: ⚠️ PARTIAL - FFE tab loads but spreadsheet is empty without rooms. Need to test with project that has rooms and items to verify 17-column structure and stock tracking.
detailed_findings.mobile_app: ❌ NOT TESTED - Mobile app simulator component exists but needs separate testing. Photo capture and offline sync features require dedicated mobile testing.
detailed_findings.dashboard_tabs: ⚠️ MIXED - All 12 tabs (Questionnaire, Walkthrough, Checklist, FF&E, Finance, Calendar, Reports, Design, Automation, Exports, Measurements, To Do) are visible in UI. However, 5 tabs have missing backend APIs: Finance, Calendar, Reports, Automation, Exports.
detailed_findings.print_exports: ❌ CRITICAL ISSUE - All 3 print export endpoints return 404. Client needs these sheets (electrician, load-in, mover's FFE) for contractors tomorrow. This is a blocking issue for real-world use.
detailed_findings.stock_tracking: ⚠️ PARTIAL - Item statuses work (35 statuses available), but carriers endpoint returns 404, so carrier dropdown will not populate.
detailed_findings.design_tools: ✅ WORKING - Paint catalog loads successfully with colors from Sherwin Williams, Benjamin Moore, and Farrow & Ball.
